claims.object_text: reduction of GABA(A) receptor beta3 subunit results in epilepsy / GABAergic role in Angelman pathophysiology
claims.quote: These gabrb3 gene knockout mice provide direct evidence that a reduction of a specific subunit of the GABA(A) receptor system can result in epilepsy and support a GABAergic role in the pathophysiology of Angelman syndrome.

The GABA(A) receptor beta3 subunit gene, gabrb3/GABRB3 (mouse/human), is of particular interest because of its expression early in development and its possible role in the neurodevelopmental disorder Angelman syndrome.
